products.name: Lovo (Genny)
products.note: Voice cloning and synthesis; likeness consent; commercial voiceover; synthetic media disclosure

reading.body:
Lovo is a voice cloning and synthesis company whose product, Genny, is built around likeness consent and synthetic media disclosure.

The data covers one product in one category, voice and audio. It records the compliance posture, consent for likeness and disclosure of synthetic media, but not the model architecture, the training data, or the compute behind it. Nothing here indicates whether Lovo trains its own models or rents inference from someone else, which is the distinction that decides where its costs sit.

For AI scaling, voice synthesis is a lighter load than image or video generation, so this page does not bear directly on the grid constraint. What it does show is that the consent and disclosure layer is now part of the product description itself, not a legal footnote. That is a regulatory signal rather than an infrastructure one.

The data is thin on numbers. There are no prices, no usage figures, no dates beyond the page generation, and no case studies. It should be read as a company identity record, not as evidence about Lovo's scale or its draw on compute.
